title: The Man With the Headache That Wouldn't Add Up — Body Pains, Tingling, and Twenty Years of Whiskey

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 41 years old, presenting with headache and generalized body pains for the past three months, with a history of trauma. He had been apparently well four months before this, when he developed the headache and body pains, along with intermittent giddiness, intermittent numbness and tingling in his hands and feet, and multiple other somatic complaints. He denies fever, convulsions, loss of consciousness, or vomiting and loose stools.

He has no known history of hypertension, diabetes, tuberculosis, asthma, or epilepsy. He eats a mixed diet, with regular bowel and bladder habits. He has been drinking whiskey regularly for 20 years, about 180 ml a day.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **General exam:** conscious, coherent, and cooperative; no pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, koilonychia, generalized lymphadenopathy, or edema
- **Vitals:** blood pressure 130/100 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, respiratory rate 16/min, temperature 98.4°F
- **Systemic exam:** heart sounds S1 and S2 normal; bilateral air entry present on chest exam; abdomen soft and non-tender; no abnormality detected on neurological exam

sections.heading: How the Story Unfolded on the Ward
sections.content: Given his 20-year history of heavy daily whiskey intake alongside tobacco use, and the constellation of headache, diffuse body pains, and intermittent paresthesias without any localizing findings on examination, he was diagnosed with alcohol and tobacco dependence syndrome, with a possible underlying dysthymia being considered.
